Project.name: Agent Lab
Project.annotation: A tool for running and testing agentic systems in isolation. It runs OpenCode in a sandbox ("vacuum") with controlled settings and lets you observe how an agent behaves under varied system prompts, models, and task prompts. Multiple instances can run in parallel or one at a time. Primary consumers are agents that invoke the tool to test prompts and inspect behavior; humans are a secondary, later concern.
Project.keywords: agent, lab, llm, orchestration, sandbox, prompt, tests, opencode, configuration, tools

Actors.actor-Agent: Primary actor: an external AI agent (e.g. Claude, OpenCode) that invokes Agent Lab to run experiments and inspect agent behavior.
Actors.actor-Operator: Secondary actor: a human operator running experiments and reviewing results from the CLI. Lower priority for v1.
Actors.actor-System: Internal actor: background orchestration that provisions sandboxes, drives OpenCode, and collects traces.

UC-001.Action: Runs an experiment with a chosen system prompt, model, and task prompt
UC-001.Goal: To observe how the OpenCode agent behaves under those exact settings, inside an isolated sandbox
UC-001.Preconditions: OpenCode is available; a provider/model and credentials are configured; a sandbox can be provisioned.
UC-001.AcceptanceCriteria: A run is created, executed to completion (or timeout), and a behavior trace (steps, tool-calls, tokens, timings, final output) is captured and retrievable by run id.

UC-002.Action: Runs several experiments in parallel with different settings
UC-002.Goal: To compare agent behavior across system-prompt / model / task variations without cross-interference
UC-002.Preconditions: Each run gets its own isolated sandbox; host has capacity for N parallel containers.
UC-002.AcceptanceCriteria: N runs execute concurrently in separate sandboxes; no run can observe or mutate another run's filesystem or session; each produces an independent trace.

UC-003.Action: Retrieves and compares the results/traces of completed runs
UC-003.Goal: To reason about which prompt/model variant behaved best
UC-003.Preconditions: Runs have completed and traces are persisted.
UC-003.AcceptanceCriteria: Listing returns known runs; fetching a run returns its full trace; comparing two or more runs returns a structured diff of behavior/outcome.

UC-004.Action: Drives the same experiments from a human-facing CLI
UC-004.Goal: To run and inspect experiments manually
UC-004.Preconditions: Same core engine as agent-driven usage.
UC-004.AcceptanceCriteria: CLI exposes run/list/show/compare over the same engine the agent uses; human readability is secondary to v1.

NonGoals.item-1: No multi-agent backend in v1 — the tool is built around OpenCode specifically, not a universal agent adapter.
NonGoals.item-2: No MCP or HTTP interface in v1 — CLI only. The core engine is kept separate so MCP/HTTP can wrap it later.
NonGoals.item-3: No rich human UI/dashboard in v1 — humans are a secondary concern.
NonGoals.item-4: No dependency on third-party sandbox/agent-runner products (vibekit, rivet sandbox-agent, E2B, Daytona) as the foundation; ideas may be borrowed, but the core is owned.
NonGoals.item-5: No production multi-tenant scaling concerns in v1 (single-host, local Docker).

Constraints.constraint-1: Each instance must run isolated from the host and from other instances ("vacuum"): isolated filesystem and a constrained network surface.
Constraints.constraint-2: The agent inside the sandbox still needs outbound access to the configured LLM API endpoint; the "vacuum" means deny-by-default networking with an explicit allowlist for that endpoint only.
Constraints.constraint-3: OpenCode is the only agent runtime in scope; it is driven via the headless server (opencode serve) and @opencode-ai/sdk.
Constraints.constraint-4: Secrets, credentials, and raw provider tokens must never appear in logs or persisted traces (redaction borrowed from the vibekit idea).
Constraints.constraint-5: The tool itself is built on Bun + TypeScript to align with the OpenCode ecosystem.

Risks.risk-1: "Vacuum" vs. required LLM access is a tension: too strict a network policy breaks the agent; too loose breaks isolation. The allowlist must be exact and tested.
Risks.risk-2: OpenCode SDK / server surface is evolving; OpenCode-driving code must be isolated behind one adapter module to absorb churn.
Risks.risk-3: Agent behavior is non-deterministic; trace capture and comparison must tolerate variance and still produce stable, structured evidence.
Risks.risk-4: Parallel sandboxes consume significant host resources (CPU, memory, disk); concurrency must be bounded and observable.
Risks.risk-5: Container lifecycle leaks (orphaned containers/volumes) on crash or timeout; teardown must be guaranteed.

OpenQuestions.resolved-1: Behavior trace = RunTrace owned by M-TRACE: runId, experiment, status, timings, steps[], tokenUsage, finalOutput(text + git diff), error?.
OpenQuestions.resolved-2: Provider credentials injected via env at docker run; redacted in logs and persisted traces. No credential broker in v1.
OpenQuestions.resolved-3: Persistence is flat JSON under runs/<runId>/{run.json, trace.json, raw.log}; SQLite deferred.
OpenQuestions.resolved-4: Bounded parallelism, default 4, overridable via --concurrency, soft-capped by host resources.
OpenQuestions.resolved-5: Experiment input accepted both inline (CLI args) and via a config file (variation matrix).
OpenQuestions.resolved-6: Runs are replayable: ExperimentDefinition persists with the run; agent-lab run --from <runId> replays it.
